meta.title: Four Timelines
meta.subtitle: The package counts four, not three — and the fourth hides behind the third whenever forced input latency is zero

views.label: The client never reads the server clock
views.note: It estimates the tick it is about to receive, and builds both of its own clocks from that estimate.

views.label: One estimate, two directions
views.note: Subtract the interpolation window for the past. Add round trip plus command slack for the future.

views.label: The fourth timeline
views.note: Input target tick is predicted tick plus effective input latency. At zero they are the same number.

views.label: When the order inverts
views.note: Enough forced latency pushes prediction behind interpolation, so the interpolation window is stretched instead.

nodes.label: Arrival estimate
nodes.sublabel: next tick we expect to receive

cards.title: The four, oldest to newest
items: Interpolation tick — what you see of everyone else
Snapshot arrival tick — the newest server state actually in hand
Server tick on the client — the tick prediction is aiming at
Input target tick — the tick your keypress is stamped with

cards.title: What collapses four into three
items: Input target equals predicted plus the effective input latency
Effective latency is zero by default, so the two coincide and you see three
It is not zero when forced input latency is configured above zero
It is also not zero when ping exceeds the maximum predict ahead time, which raises it for you

cards.title: Neither client clock is read from the server
items: The client keeps an estimate of the tick it is about to receive next
Both of its clocks are derived from that estimate, in opposite directions
Each has its own rate multiplier, nudged a fraction of the error per frame
So the clocks are servo loops, not counters, and they are allowed to run slightly fast or slow

cards.title: The inversion nobody expects
items: Enough forced latency pushes the predicted tick behind the interpolation tick
Netcode does not let the order invert
It drags the interpolation target forward to meet the predicted tick
The interpolation window silently lengthens, so tuning one knob moves the other
